title: RESCQ: Realtime Scheduling for Continuous Angle Quantum Error Correction Architectures
problem: Continuous angle quantum error correction architectures require non-deterministic resource state production, meaning statically generated schedules waste cycles when states fail and must be re-attempted. Without a realtime scheduler, execution time is unnecessarily long and classical control overhead for frequent rescheduling can dominate.
motivation: Large-scale quantum error correction is bottlenecked by expensive resource state preparation; continuous angle rotation alternatives are non-deterministic and require dynamic resource management that static scheduling cannot provide.
method: RESCQ is a realtime scheduler for continuous angle QEC architectures that actively redistributes resources on-demand based on expected production rates of rotation states. It monitors resource state generation success and, upon failure, dynamically reassigns resources from lower-priority to higher-priority operations to minimize total cycle count. To control classical control overhead, RESCQ adaptively selects the recomputation frequency based on the state of the system, reducing unnecessary scheduling invocations when the system is stable.
key_novelty: Dynamic, on-demand redistribution of quantum resources in continuous angle QEC systems with adaptive recomputation frequency to balance cycle-count minimization against classical control overhead.
contributions: RESCQ: a realtime scheduler for continuous angle rotation QEC architectures
On-demand resource redistribution based on expected production rates
Adaptive recomputation frequency to limit classical control overhead
Average 2x cycle count improvement over baseline static proposals

metrics.speedup: average 2x improvement in cycle count over baseline static proposals

baselines: statically generated schedules for continuous angle QEC architectures
limitations: Excessive classical control overhead possible on some hardware; adaptive frequency selection mitigates but does not eliminate it.
